title: Agentic Postgres project manifest
description: Non-secret deployment configuration. This file is the sole authority for the numeric bounds below; documentation is generated from it and validation code reads it rather than restating any value.

schema_version.description: Manifest format version. 1, 2 or 3. Version 2 (ADR 0183) replaces `mcp.max_result_rows` and `mcp.max_response_bytes` -- two fields nothing ever read (D929) -- with `mcp.profile`, which the lock compiler reads. A field is FORBIDDEN below the version that introduces it and REQUIRED at or above it (ADR 0177's rule, applied to this document), and the two replaced fields are the mirror image: required at 1, forbidden at 2. Version 3 (ADR 0186) adds `project.lifecycle`, required at 3 and forbidden below it; `permanent` is what every earlier version meant by omitting it. Versions 1 and 2 still load, because `project.alpha.yaml` and `project.beta.yaml` live only on the host and no commit can edit them.

domain.description: Public DNS name. No scheme, port, path, or wildcard.

lifecycle.description: Version 3 (ADR 0186). Whether this project is permanent or ephemeral, and when an ephemeral one expires. `permanent` is what every earlier version meant by saying nothing, so a version 1 or 2 manifest renders as a permanent project and no manifest needs migrating. `expires_at` is required exactly when `kind` is `ephemeral`, and is a fact an operator reads -- the inventory reports an expired project and the retirement verb refuses an unexpired one -- never a trigger: no unit, timer or cron acts on it (D951).

kind.description: `permanent` outlives every release it is deployed under; `ephemeral` is created for a purpose and retired after `expires_at`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, second precision, `Z` suffix -- the shape `observed_at` has. Required when `kind` is `ephemeral`, forbidden otherwise. Compared against the clock at render time: a project born expired is a typo.

name.description: Database name. Defaults to the SQL-safe project key.

pooled_public.description: Expose PgBouncer publicly. UNSUPPORTED as of ADR 0040: the pooler is reachable only through a loopback publication and a verified tunnel, so `true` is refused with a stable unsupported-profile error rather than honoured. The field stays declarable so that a manifest asking for it gets that answer, instead of an unknown-key error that reads like a typo.

pooled_public_cidrs.description: Source networks permitted to reach the pooler. Must be empty: there is no supported configuration in which a non-loopback source reaches the pooler directly (ADR 0040).

max_prepared_statements.description: How many protocol-level named prepared statements the pooler tracks per connection. Must be non-zero: at 0 a named statement is unusable the moment transaction pooling moves the client to a different backend, which was measured against the locked image rather than read from its documentation. This is the setting a failing client test must never be 'fixed' by lowering.

query_wait_timeout_seconds.description: How long a client may wait for a server connection before the pooler gives up. Bounded above so a saturated pool fails rather than stalling: an unbounded queue turns a capacity problem into a hang, and a hang has no error message to act on.

idle_transaction_timeout_seconds.description: How long a client may hold a server connection inside an idle transaction. Cannot be disabled here, because in transaction pooling one idle transaction holds a server connection out of the pool for as long as it lasts.

server_lifetime_seconds.description: How long a server connection is reused before the pooler retires it. Bounded above so that a rotated credential cannot be held indefinitely by a long-lived backend, and below so that recycling does not become the dominant cost.

pool_size.description: Server-side pool size. Must not exceed max_client_connections.

shared_buffers_mb.description: PostgreSQL shared_buffers. Counts in full against the memory guardrail: it is shared memory, which no swap can relieve and no cache reclaim can shrink.

max_connections.description: PostgreSQL max_connections on the cluster itself, not the pooler's ceiling. Deliberately small: Session 4's answer to connection count is a pooler, and a large per-cluster limit would make the pooler decorative. 56 since Session 7, and the six are what the storage service costs (ADR 0099) -- at 50 the budget divided exactly three ways with nothing spare, and a fourth claimant pushed the application's remainder below the pooler's own pool.

work_mem_mb.description: Per-sort-node working memory. Allocated on demand, so it does not multiply by max_connections in practice; the guardrail charges a flat per-backend anonymous allowance instead. See the Session 3 plan 3.3.

maintenance_work_mem_mb.description: VACUUM and index-build working memory. Charged in full against the guardrail because one maintenance operation can hold it for a long time.

memory_limit_mb.description: The container mem_limit. NOT the same number as the guardrail: a container limit caps page cache too, so a limit set equal to the unreclaimable budget makes the cluster live in permanent cache reclaim. Measured at 512 MiB with these defaults, two clusters pegged their limit with several hundred reclaim events and no OOM kill. Must exceed the derived unreclaimable budget.

shm_size_mb.description: The container /dev/shm size. PostgreSQL's dynamic shared memory for parallel query lands here, and Docker's 64 MiB default is below the default shared_buffers. Must be at least shared_buffers_mb.

database.comment: Through Session 3 this object carried an if/then requiring a non-empty allowlist when `pooled_public` was true. ADR 0040 removed the configuration that rule was guarding, and the rule had to go with it: combined with `maxItems: 0` it would have been unsatisfiable, so every `pooled_public: true` manifest would have failed with a schema contradiction instead of the stable unsupported-profile error that says what to do.

public_base_path.description: Route prefix for the REST and application surfaces.
Route prefix for the MCP transport.

max_result_rows.description: Schema version 1 only, and READ BY NOTHING (D929): declared as the agent read row ceiling since Session 1, it reaches neither Compose, the lock nor the runtime. Version 2 replaces it with `mcp.profile.<tool>.max_rows`, which the lock compiler reads (ADR 0183). Must not exceed api.max_rows.

max_response_bytes.description: Schema version 1 only, and READ BY NOTHING (D929). Its maximum is ten times the runtime's `MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES`, so even a reader could not have honoured it. Version 2 replaces it with `mcp.profile.<tool>.max_response_bytes`, bounded at the runtime's ceiling (ADR 0183).

profile.description: Schema version 2 (ADR 0183). This project's narrowing of the approved capability contract, keyed by tool name. **A profile may only NARROW** (D867): every value is compared against what the approved contract compiles for that tool when the lock is compiled, and a value that would widen any bound -- or that names a tool the contract does not compile, or a field the tool's kind does not carry -- fails `bin/mcp-contract.sh check --project` and the deploy's lock step, before a deployment exists. Nothing is clamped. An empty object is a project that narrows nothing, stated rather than absent. The vocabulary is the seven bounds the runtime reads from the lock and nothing else; a profile cannot remove a tool, narrow a column list, or touch a per-capability declaration.

bucket.description: R2 bucket. Defaults to `apg-{project_key}` -- namespaced like every other derived identifier here, because a bucket's collision domain is the whole Cloudflare account and a bare project key sits in the same namespace as whatever else that account holds (ADR 0105, D339). A value given HERE is used verbatim and is not prefixed: the override exists so an operator can point at a bucket named by a convention that is not ours, and prefixing it would defeat the only reason it exists. A collision on an overridden name is the operator's to resolve, and the bootstrap still refuses to adopt a bucket it did not create.

prefix.description: Relative object prefix ending in '/'. Defaults to objects/{project_key}/.

account_id.description: The Cloudflare account the bucket lives in, 32 lowercase hex characters. Required when storage is enabled and forbidden when it is not. This is an IDENTIFIER, not a credential -- it appears in the endpoint hostname of every request and in the dashboard URL -- so it is a manifest field rather than a secret: putting a non-credential through per-consumer materialization would spend the machinery that makes 'one service cannot read another's credential' a filesystem property on a value that is not one, and would make the endpoint unresolvable at --render-only time (ADR 0106). The endpoint is derived from it by naming.storage_endpoint_url and handed to the container as STORAGE_ENDPOINT; it is never assembled a second time inside the image.

jurisdiction.description: The R2 jurisdiction the bucket was created in. A jurisdictional bucket is reachable ONLY through its own endpoint host, and most S3 clients hold one endpoint per client, so this belongs to the endpoint derivation rather than being a label. Only 'default' has been measured -- Run 5's probe bucket reports jurisdiction 'default' and every arm of the rig dialled its endpoint. The other two are READ FROM VENDOR DOCUMENTATION and have never been dialled by anything here; the enum is closed at what Cloudflare documents today and says so rather than implying all three are proved (ADR 0106).

upload_url_ttl_seconds.description: Presigned upload URL lifetime. A presigned URL is a bearer credential with a short life, so this is the residual exposure of one issued URL -- it is not revoked by a later tombstone, and the documentation says so plainly rather than implying otherwise.

download_url_ttl_seconds.description: Presigned download URL lifetime. Shorter than the upload default because an upload is one deliberate act by the holder and a download URL is the one that ends up pasted somewhere.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest accepted upload. P0 default is 25 MiB.

memory_limit_mb.description: The storage container's memory limit. 384 is the application API's figure, INHERITED RATHER THAN MEASURED. A second application container's memory floor is listed as 'must be measured' in this session's feasibility table and cannot be until there is an adapter to measure; it is a manifest field precisely so the number stays visible and overridable while it is provisional, rather than being a literal nobody knows is unmeasured. ADR 0082 is the shape that measurement has to take -- one profile per process with a no-work control, because ru_maxrss is a high-water mark already set by earlier work and reports the same plausible number for every row.

pool_size.description: The storage service's cluster pool (Session 7, ADR 0099). Charged against database.max_connections as pool_size + 2 reserved, whether or not storage is enabled -- a division that moved when somebody toggled a flag would make the bootstrap plane's arithmetic depend on a flag it does not read. Raising it lowers what is left for the application, and the bootstrap refuses when that remainder falls below database.pool_size, because the pooler cannot fill a pool larger than the role's own CONNECTION LIMIT.

allowed_cors_origins.description: Exact HTTPS origins a browser may reach the storage surface from. The same pattern api.rest.allowed_cors_origins uses, and the same refusals in one place: a path, a query, a fragment, a wildcard, a userinfo component, plain http, and the literal `null` that a sandboxed iframe and a file:// document send. This is the ONE origin list for storage; the edge middleware and the bucket's own CORS policy are two renderings of it (ADR 0085's ground, D323).

stanza.description: pgBackRest stanza. Defaults to the project key.

bucket.description: The R2 bucket holding the pgBackRest repository. Defaults to `apg-{project_key}-backup`, namespaced like every other derived identifier (ADR 0105 applied, not restated), and a value given HERE is used verbatim and unprefixed for the same reason storage.bucket's override is. A SEPARATE bucket from storage.bucket, and that is ADR 0145 rather than a filing choice: R2 scopes an API token to buckets far more cleanly than to key prefixes, so 'the storage service cannot reach the backup repository' becomes a token scope a HeadBucket can be measured against instead of a policy sentence nothing executes.

account_id.description: The Cloudflare account the backup bucket lives in, 32 lowercase hex characters. Required when backups are enabled and forbidden when they are not. An IDENTIFIER and not a credential, exactly as storage.account_id is: it appears in the endpoint hostname of every request, so it is a manifest field rather than a secret, and the endpoint is derived from it by naming.storage_endpoint_url -- the same function, not a second one (ADR 0002, ADR 0106). Declared separately from storage.account_id so a repository can live in a different account from application objects; nothing here requires them to differ, and nothing requires them to match.

jurisdiction.description: The R2 jurisdiction the backup bucket was created in. storage.jurisdiction's paragraph applies unchanged: a jurisdictional bucket is reachable only through its own endpoint host, only 'default' has ever been dialled by anything here, and the enum is closed at what Cloudflare documents rather than at what has been proved.

retain_full.description: Full backup chains retained, rendered into the repository's `repo1-retention-full`. Two is what docs/source-specification.md section 12.1 asks for. This bound existed from Session 1 and was read by NO code until Session 10 -- no default resolution, no propagation, absent from outputs.json (D519) -- so a manifest could set it to 7 and nothing would retain seven chains.

appService.description: The application API service, Session 6: the auth service, served under `api.public_base_path` + `/app`. Declared separately from `rest` because the two commit separately to the cluster's connection budget, and ADR 0070 exists because granting the same headroom to two claimants independently is how a budget comes to sum past what the server will hand out. Optional as a whole, like `rest`. The Argon2id profile is NOT declared here -- it is frozen in the service (ADR 0081), because a profile a manifest could weaken is not a frozen one -- but the memory limit that has to accommodate it is, because a container limit is a property of this deployment while the profile is a property of the product.

pool_size.description: Connections the auth service's psycopg pool may hold. Charged to the cluster's budget whether or not the service is enabled, for the reason `resolve_api_connection_budget` gives about REST: a division that depended on whether a service happened to be on would move when somebody toggled it.

memory_limit_mb.description: The auth container's memory limit, in MiB. This minimum is a floor on the field; the real bound is ADR 0082's cross-field relation, which requires `hash_concurrency` x `memory_cost` plus the service's process overhead to fit -- so a manifest declaring too little fails validation rather than being killed by the OOM killer at the first burst of logins. Measured in Run 7: 67.1 MiB resident per concurrent hash at the frozen profile, linear in concurrency (131.1 at two, 259.0 at four), against a no-hash control that moved the resident figure by 0.0; and 60.9 MiB for the process with every dependency imported and an application object built.

restService.description: The PostgREST service, Session 5. Optional as a whole: a project manifest written before this session names no REST service, and a project that does not declare one publishes `routes.rest: unavailable` rather than failing to render. `api.max_rows` stays the sole row-limit authority and is deliberately NOT repeated here.

request_body_max_bytes.description: Largest accepted request body. Bounded above because the edge buffers what it accepts, and equal to request_body_memory_bytes for P0 so an accepted body stays in memory rather than spilling to proxy disk -- a spilled body is a request payload written to a filesystem nobody is auditing.

request_body_memory_bytes.description: How much of a request body the edge holds in memory. Must equal request_body_max_bytes; the pair exists because the two are separately configurable at the edge and a smaller memory limit is how bodies reach disk.

pool_size.description: PostgREST's own connection pool, against the DIRECT transport rather than the pooler: it needs prepared statements and a LISTEN/NOTIFY channel for the schema cache, neither of which survives transaction pooling. Counted against database.max_connections together with the pooler's server pool and an administration reserve.

pool_acquisition_timeout_seconds.description: How long a request waits for a connection before failing. Bounded above for the reason the pooler's queue timeout is: a request that waits without limit turns a capacity problem into a hang, and a hang has no error message to act on.

pool_max_idle_seconds.description: How long an unused pooled connection is kept. Must be less than pool_max_lifetime_seconds.

pool_max_lifetime_seconds.description: How long a pooled connection is reused before it is retired. Bounded above so a rotated credential cannot be held indefinitely by a long-lived connection -- the same reason database.server_lifetime_seconds is bounded.

anonymous_access.description: A frozen enumeration with one member. `anon` exists so an unauthenticated request has a role to be, not so that it can read: migration 0004 grants it nothing. The field is a single-valued enum rather than absent so that a manifest asking for anything else is refused by name instead of accepted as an unknown key.

allowed_cors_origins.description: Exact HTTPS origins: scheme, host, optional port, and nothing else. The pattern refuses a path, a query, a fragment, a wildcard, a userinfo component and the literal `null` in one place -- `null` is the origin a sandboxed iframe and a file:// document send, and an allowlist containing it is an allowlist that admits anything that can arrange to be opaque.

additionalProperties.description: A strict duration: digits and a unit, no space, no compound, no zero. PostgreSQL reads a bare integer as milliseconds and `0` as *disabled*, so a grammar that admitted either would let a manifest turn the timeout off by looking like it set one.

statement_timeouts.description: Per-role statement_timeout, keyed by the platform role suffix. Only roles that exist may be named, which is checked against `naming.ROLE_SUFFIXES` rather than enumerated here: a timeout set on a role nothing created is a setting that never applies and never says so.

profileEntry.title: tool
profileEntry.description: One tool's narrowing (ADR 0183). The seven fields are exactly the bounds the runtime reads from the lock; each applies to the kinds named in `capability_compiler.PROFILE_FIELDS`, and the compiler refuses a field on a kind that does not carry it. The ranges here mirror the capability schema's so that a profile cannot even ask for more than a capability may declare; the real refusal is the comparison against the compiled contract, which no schema can express. `minProperties: 1` because an empty entry reads as a restriction and applies none.

timeout_ms.description: At most the tool's compiled `timeout_ms`. Applies to every kind.

max_response_bytes.description: At most the tool's compiled `max_response_bytes`. Reads and writes only; the maximum is the runtime's `MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES`, as in the capability schema (ADR 0179).

max_concurrent_calls.description: At most the tool's compiled `max_concurrent_calls`. Reads and writes only.

max_rows.description: At most EVERY resource's compiled `max_rows` behind a read tool -- `query_resource` has two and they may disagree, so a per-tool value is checked against each. Reads only. Must not exceed api.max_rows.

max_affected_rows.description: At most the write's compiled `max_affected_rows`. Writes only.

supports_dry_run.description: A PERMISSION, so `false` is the narrow end: a profile may withdraw a dry run the contract supports and may not grant one it does not. Writes only.

requires_approval.description: A RESTRICTION, so `true` is the narrow end: a profile may require approval where the contract does not and may not lift a requirement the contract declares. Writes only.

allOf.description: The version 2 gate (ADR 0183), at the document level for ADR 0177's reason: a manifest declaring one version and carrying the other's shape is the state this exists to refuse. `profile` is required at 2 rather than optional, so a version 2 manifest that narrows nothing says so with an empty object instead of by omission; the two fields it replaces are forbidden at 2 so that a reader never sees an inert bound beside a live one.

The version 3 gate (ADR 0186), ADR 0177's rule again: `project.lifecycle` is required at 3 and forbidden below it. Below 3 a manifest says nothing and means permanent; at 3 it says so. A manifest declaring 2 and carrying a lifecycle is the state this refuses -- a field read by a version the manifest does not claim to be.
